attribution.note: Marcus states this prediction directly in his own list.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the firm prediction, first-time qualifier and 2026 midterm horizon. The surrounding backlash discussion supplies no conditional antecedent.

contract.note: Meaningful campaign and voter salience is a fair ordinary reading of an election issue. Comparing earlier national election cycles reasonably preserves the novelty claim, although Marcus supplies no explicit salience threshold.

evidence.note: Dated polling supports substantial voter interest in AI during the 2026 midterms. It does not establish historical novelty.
Advertising measurements establish data-center campaigning, but do not separate AI-related messages from other infrastructure concerns.
Contemporaneous reporting documents substantive AI campaign messaging. It supports the 2026 component but cannot establish first-time salience.

Yang's interview documents substantive earlier campaigning about AI and automation. Without comparable voter or broader campaign evidence, it does not establish earlier electoral salience under the contract.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports AI's emergence as a 2026 campaign issue but neither establishes nor refutes comparable salience in earlier cycles. Yang's interview is relevant but insufficient to settle novelty. The November 3 deadline remains ahead of the October 28 cutoff, and neither early-resolution condition is met.
